leather noun and adjective

classical

Traupman 117
M-O s.v. cloth, types: leather

corium, coriī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Other words

  • scorteus, scortea, scorteum — leather, of leather

    also used · classical · Traupman 117; M-O s.v. cloth, types: leather; Traupman 338 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • coriaceus — of leather

    also used · late Latin · M-O s.v. cloth, types: leather

  • scortum, scortī n. — a skin, hide

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Varr. LL 7.84 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 117 · Declension on Wiktionary

    “Hide” only in Varro; its ordinary sense is a prostitute. Use corium or the adjective scorteus.

Examples

  • ex coriō

    made of leatherTraupman 338

See also fur, raincoat.
